name: Sheet Pan Lemon Herb Salmon with Green Beans, Broccoli and Carrots
flavorProfile: Salmon brushed with lemon, garlic and herb butter, baked on one sheet pan with green beans, broccoli and carrots.
healthBenefit: Salmon brings omega-3 fats, and the green beans, broccoli and carrots roast on the same pan, so the whole meal comes off one tray.

ingredients.prepNote: dried; part of the Italian seasoning
dried; part of the Italian seasoning
dried; part of the Italian seasoning
dried; part of the Italian seasoning
coarse; half for the salmon, half for the vegetables
half for the salmon, half for the vegetables

instructions: Heat the oven to 400F (200C) and grease a rimmed baking pan.
Stir the melted butter, garlic, lemon juice, Italian seasoning and half the salt and pepper together in a small bowl.
Toss the green beans, broccoli and carrots on the pan with the olive oil and the rest of the salt and pepper. Spread them out and bake for 15 minutes.
Push the vegetables aside, lay the salmon in the space, brush it with the butter mixture and drizzle what is left over the vegetables.
Bake for 15 to 18 minutes more, until the salmon flakes easily with a fork. Take care not to overcook it.
Garnish with lemon slices and parsley and serve right away.

name: Halibut on Carrots, Parsley Root and Peas
flavorProfile: Pan-fried halibut over carrots, parsley root and peas, finished with fresh parsley.
healthBenefit: Halibut brings protein, and the carrots, parsley root and peas are cooked briefly in a covered pan with a little oil and water.

ingredients.prepNote: for the vegetables and the fish

instructions: Heat 1 teaspoon of the oil in a pan and sweat the carrot and parsley root slices for 3 minutes.
Add the peas and the water, cover, and cook for 5 minutes. Stir in the parsley and season with half the salt and pepper.
Season the fish with the rest of the salt and pepper. Heat the remaining oil in a second pan and fry the fish for 2 minutes on each side.
Serve the fish on the vegetables.

name: Roasted Cod with Fennel and Lemon
flavorProfile: Baked cod fillet with roasted fennel and zucchini, finished with lemon and avocado.
healthBenefit: Lean cod roasted on a tray of fennel and tomatoes, a light whole-food plate with very little saturated fat.

ingredients.prepNote: half a bulb, fronds kept for garnish
for the vegetables, plus a pinch on the cod
for the vegetables, plus a pinch on the cod

instructions: Heat the oven to 400F (200C).
Toss the fennel and tomatoes on a baking sheet with half the olive oil, the lemon juice, the salt and the pepper. Roast for 20 minutes.
Season the cod with a pinch of salt and pepper and lay it among the vegetables with the lemon slices.
Roast for 10 to 12 minutes more, until the cod flakes easily.
Drizzle the rest of the olive oil over the top, scatter the fennel fronds and serve.

name: Zesty Shrimp and Cabbage Stir-Fry
flavorProfile: Shrimp seared in toasted sesame oil, then tossed with cabbage, carrot, garlic and ginger in a coconut aminos, lime and sriracha sauce.
healthBenefit: A one-pan dinner for one: the shrimp cooks in about four minutes and the vegetables keep some crunch.

ingredients.baseName: Onions, spring or scallions (includes tops and bulb)

instructions: Pat the shrimp dry and season them with the salt and pepper.
Heat the sesame oil in a large skillet or wok over medium-high heat. Sear the shrimp about 2 minutes on each side, until pink, then lift them onto a plate.
Add the garlic and ginger to the pan and stir for about 30 seconds, until fragrant.
Add the cabbage and carrot and stir-fry 3 to 4 minutes, until they soften but keep a little crunch.
Whisk the coconut aminos, lime juice and sriracha together in a small bowl.
Return the shrimp to the pan, pour in the sauce and toss for about 1 minute, until everything is coated and hot.
Serve topped with the green onion and sesame seeds.

name: Beef Sirloin with Braised Greens, Baby Carrots and Herb Olive Oil
flavorProfile: Seared and roasted beef sirloin over garlicky wilted chard and spinach, with roasted baby carrots and a fresh herb oil.
healthBenefit: Beef top sirloin brings iron, and the chard and spinach are wilted in a pan for a minute or two rather than served raw.

ingredients.prepNote: kosher; ¼ tsp for the steak, the rest for the carrots and greens
minced; for the greens and the herb oil
for searing, the carrots, the greens and the herb oil

instructions: Heat the oven to 400F (200C). Mix the parsley, tarragon, chives, most of the minced garlic, the orange zest and 1 tablespoon of the olive oil to make the herb oil.
Season the steak with the salt, cracked pepper and granulated garlic. Sear it in a little oil in a hot ovenproof pan for 3 minutes, turn it and sear 1 minute more.
Move the pan to the oven and roast until the center reaches 120F (49C) for medium rare. Rest the steak for 15 minutes before slicing.
Toss the baby carrots with a little oil and a pinch of salt and pepper and roast them alongside until tender.
Warm the last of the oil in a pan, add the rest of the garlic, then the chard and spinach. Cook for 1 to 2 minutes, until just wilted, and season with a pinch of salt and pepper.
Serve the sliced steak over the greens with the carrots, spooning the herb oil over the top.

name: Pork Tenderloin with Braised Cabbage & Apple
flavorProfile: Spice-rubbed roast pork tenderloin over butter-braised cabbage, topped with apples cooked in cider.
healthBenefit: Lean pork tenderloin with cabbage and apple, a classic pairing built from whole foods.

ingredients.baseName: Apple juice, canned or bottled, without added vitamin C

instructions: Mix most of the salt with the pepper, coriander, cinnamon, and nutmeg, and rub it over the pork. Roast at 400°F (200°C) for 20-25 minutes, until it reaches 145°F (63°C), then rest for a few minutes before slicing.
Meanwhile, melt a quarter of the butter in a covered pan, add the cabbage and a pinch of the salt, and cook over medium-low heat for 12-15 minutes, stirring now and then, until soft.
In another pan, melt the remaining butter, add the apple and shallot with the last of the salt, and cook until the apple is tender. Add the cider and thyme and cook until the cider has nearly gone.
Serve the sliced pork over the cabbage with the apples on top.

name: Salmon, Fennel & Leek Soup
flavorProfile: A light soup of salmon poached in vegetable broth with fennel, leek, carrot, shiitake and spinach.
healthBenefit: Salmon brings protein and omega-3 fat to a light broth of fennel, leek, carrot, celery, mushrooms and spinach, started in a little butter.
instructions: Melt the butter in a heavy pot over medium high heat.
Add the carrot, celery, fennel, leek, thyme, salt and pepper and stir. Cook 5 to 7 minutes, until the vegetables start to wilt.
Pour in the vegetable stock and water and bring just to a low boil, then turn the heat to low.
Add the mushrooms and simmer 10 to 12 minutes, stirring now and then.

Add the salmon and spinach and push them under the broth. Take the pot off the heat, cover, and leave about 5 minutes, until the spinach wilts and the salmon turns from bright orange to pale and is cooked through.
Ladle into a bowl and scatter with the parsley.

name: Shrimp Lettuce Wraps with Avocado & Lime
flavorProfile: Shrimp roasted with a little olive oil, wrapped in lettuce with sliced avocado and a squeeze of lime.
healthBenefit: Shrimp, lettuce, and avocado all check completely clean for Hashimoto's, and the lettuce leaf stands in for a wrap without any grain at all.

ingredients.prepNote: juice of a quarter of a lime

instructions: Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C) and line a baking tray with parchment.
Toss the shrimp with the olive oil and salt and leave them for 10 minutes.
Spread the shrimp out on the tray and roast for 5 to 7 minutes, until opaque all the way through.
Fill the lettuce leaves with the shrimp, sliced avocado and chopped cilantro.
Squeeze the lime juice over the top and eat straight away.

name: Sirloin Steak with Shaved Fennel Salad
flavorProfile: Seared sirloin sliced over shaved raw fennel and parsley in a lemon, garlic and chili flake dressing.
healthBenefit: Sirloin brings protein, iron and zinc, and the raw fennel and parsley add fiber and vitamin C under an olive oil and lemon dressing.

ingredients.prepNote: 1 tsp for the dressing, plus about ⅓ tsp to season the steak
⅓ cup for the dressing, plus a little for the pan
½ cup leaves with tender stems

instructions: Shave the fennel thinly with a mandoline or a sharp knife and put it in a large bowl.
Whisk the garlic, lemon zest, lemon juice, mustard, sugar, the ⅓ cup olive oil, red pepper flakes and 1 teaspoon sea salt in a small bowl.
Pour the dressing over the fennel, add the parsley, toss to coat and set aside.
Season the steak generously with sea salt.
Heat a skillet over high heat with a little olive oil and cook the steak 3 to 5 minutes a side, depending on its thickness and how done you like it.
Rest the steak on a board for 5 minutes, then slice it against the grain about ¼ inch thick.
Divide the fennel salad between two plates, lay the steak on top, spoon over any resting juices and serve right away.

name: Coconut Rice Bowl with Roasted Zucchini, Pepper & Tomato
flavorProfile: Rice simmered in coconut milk, topped with roasted zucchini, bell pepper, and tomato.
healthBenefit: Rice, coconut milk, zucchini, bell pepper, and tomato all check completely clean for Hashimoto's, a genuinely hearty vegan main.
instructions: Bring the coconut milk, water and salt to a boil, stir in the rice, then cover and simmer on low for 35-45 minutes without stirring, until the rice is tender and only a little liquid is left.
Take the pan off the heat and let it stand, covered, for 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, roast the zucchini and bell pepper at 400°F (200°C) for 15-18 minutes, until tender.
Stir the cilantro and lime juice into the rice, then spoon the roasted vegetables and diced tomato over it.

name: Coconut Vegetable Soup with Fennel & Leek
flavorProfile: A light coconut-milk soup of fennel, leek, zucchini and carrot, warmed with ginger and turmeric.
healthBenefit: Fennel, leek, zucchini and carrot softened in coconut oil, simmered with ginger and turmeric and finished with coconut milk make a warming vegan soup.
instructions: Warm the coconut oil in a pot over medium heat. Add the leek, fennel and ginger and cook for about 5 minutes, stirring, until the leek softens.
Add the carrot, zucchini and turmeric and stir for 1 minute.
Pour in the water, bring to a simmer and cook for 15-18 minutes, until the vegetables are tender.
Stir in the coconut milk, salt and pepper and heat for 2 minutes without boiling.
Blend until smooth, as the source does, or leave it chunky, and serve.

name: Avocado, Fennel & Citrus Salad
flavorProfile: Thinly sliced avocado and fennel with radicchio, orange and grapefruit segments and mint, in a lemon and Dijon dressing.
healthBenefit: A bright, no-cook salad of avocado, fennel, radicchio and citrus, the fennel softened for 15 minutes in the dressing first.
instructions: Whisk the lemon juice and zest, garlic, maple syrup, mustard and most of the salt, then slowly whisk in the olive oil until it thickens.
Toss the fennel with about half the dressing and let it sit for 15 minutes to soften, then toss the radicchio in the same bowl.
Spread the fennel and radicchio on a plate, add the orange and grapefruit segments, then the avocado and mint.
Drizzle with the rest of the dressing and finish with the black pepper and the last pinch of salt.

name: Sorghum Bowl with Roasted Zucchini & Bell Pepper
flavorProfile: Tender sorghum stirred with warm coconut milk, lime and cilantro, topped with roasted zucchini and bell pepper.
healthBenefit: Sorghum, coconut milk, zucchini, and bell pepper all check completely clean for Hashimoto's, a genuinely different whole-grain base from rice.

ingredients.prepNote: juice of a quarter of a lime

instructions: Simmer the sorghum in about 180ml of water, covered, for about 1 hour, until tender with no starchy bite, adding a splash more water if it dries out. Drain any water left.
Meanwhile heat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Toss the zucchini and bell pepper with the olive oil, the pepper and a pinch of the salt and roast for 20-25 minutes, tossing halfway.
Stir the warm coconut milk, lime juice, cilantro, cumin and the rest of the salt into the sorghum and let it sit a few minutes to soak up the coconut milk.
Spoon into a bowl and top with the roasted vegetables.

name: Tomato Fennel Coconut Soup
flavorProfile: Tomato, fennel, leek and garlic roasted with thyme, then simmered in coconut milk, blended and finished with fresh cilantro.
healthBenefit: Roasting the tomato, fennel and leek first deepens their flavor before coconut milk turns them into a rich vegan soup.
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C (400°F). Spread the tomato, fennel, leek and garlic on a lined tray, toss with the olive oil, salt and pepper, and scatter the thyme over.
Roast for 20-25 minutes, until soft and lightly browned.
Tip the vegetables and their juices into a pot, add the coconut milk and bring to a gentle simmer for 5 minutes.
Blend until smooth, then stir in the cilantro and serve.

name: Avocado & Rice Lettuce Wraps
flavorProfile: Simmered brown rice folded into mashed avocado with garlic, lime and cilantro, spooned into lettuce leaves.
healthBenefit: Rice, avocado and lettuce make a simple whole-food meal, and the lettuce leaf stands in for a wrap without any gluten at all.
instructions: Simmer the brown rice in the water, covered, for about 40 minutes, until tender and the water is absorbed, then let it cool a little.
Mash the avocado with a fork until smooth, then stir in the garlic, coriander, salt, cilantro and lime juice.
Fold in the rice until it is evenly coated.
Spoon the rice into the lettuce leaves and serve right away.
